subject: ML usage & DPA: opt-out evidence and export routing
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lee <sara.lee@catalysthealth.com>, procurement@catalysthealth.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: ML usage & DPA: opt-out evidence and export routing

Hi Sara / Catalyst procurement team,

Thanks for sending over the initial DPA draft last week. We took a pass with Legal and Ops and flagged a few items we expect you'd want clarity on before committing:

- No-training / no-improvement clause: Catalyst asked for explicit "no-training" on customer content. We can commit to not using tenant data to update public or customer-facing model weights, but procurement typically asks for evidence and an operational path (e.g., onshore routing, ephemeral KV, or export-only traces).
- Prompt/response ownership: we treat prompts and generated responses as customer data for customers who opt into that entitlement. For other accounts we have standard output licensing.
- Export & residency routing: we can agree on an SFTP export lane or onshore KMS routing for proof artifacts.

Can you confirm whether you need (A) an operational attestation document, (B) a copy of the runtime export logs delivered to an SFTP, or (C) both? Attached is a short summary from our privacy team with proposed evidence options.

Proposed next step: if you confirm (A/B/C) we will: 1) produce a redlines_response doc answering the specific DPA items, 2) pull a sample export package (SFTP bundle with metadata) to demonstrate format, and 3) schedule a 30-min call with Ops to walk through routing and KMS.

Attachment: Redwood_privacy_evidence_options.pdf (summary, pdf)

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Most-Trusted Integrations, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134

From: Sara Lee <sara.lee@catalysthealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ML usage & DPA: opt-out evidence and export routing

Marcus,

Thanks — appreciate the quick summary. Attaching our redlines (Catalyst_DPA_Redlines.pdf). A few clarifying Qs from Legal and InfoSec:

1) When you say "not used to update public or customer-facing model weights", can you confirm whether that includes internal continuous improvement pipelines (telemetry/metric-driven retraining) or only model-weight updates triggered by fine-tuning runs? We need the scope tight for our compliance committee.

2) For "prompt/response ownership" — our lawyers want a short clause that says Catalyst retains title to prompts and generated outputs for customers who opt-in; for other customers they accept the standard output license. Is that a covenable wording for the DPA addendum?

3) Evidence format: preference is both (A) attestation (signed by vendor) and (B) a one-time SFTP export sample that contains: hashed prompt ids, timestamps, route metadata, and a manifest. Delivery can be to our secure SFTP. Can Redwood commit to a 1-week turnaround on the sample?

We are targeting an executive procurement signoff by Jan 5, so timeline is tight.

Attachment: Catalyst_DPA_Redlines.pdf (pdf)

—Sara
Sara Lee
Sr. Counsel, Procurement — Catalyst Health
sara.lee@catalysthealth.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 10:24:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Re: ML usage & DPA: opt-out evidence and export routing

Marcus / Dylan,

I reviewed Sara's redlines and InfoSec's ask. Short answers and operational plan below — I'll collate into a redline-responses doc and attach the operational runbook excerpt.

1) Scope of "no-train": we can offer a bounded non-learning commitment that covers two categories: 
   - No incorporation into public foundation model retraining (company-wide weight updates).
   - No feeding into automated customer-facing fine-tuning pipelines for Catalyst tenant data.
We will still collect telemetry for system health (anonymized metrics) unless they require absolute telemetry suppression — if they do, that is a separate SOW.

2) Prompt/response ownership clause: Legal suggests the following phrasing for the addendum: "Customer retains ownership of prompts and generated outputs where Customer has expressly opted into 'Customer output ownership' in the Ordering Document; otherwise, standard Redwood output license applies." I will bake that into the redline-responses doc.

3) Evidence delivery & timeline:
   - Attestation: We can produce a signed attestation covering non-learning and routing practices within 3 business days after signoff of the DPA addendum.
   - SFTP export sample: Ops can generate a one-time sample package (manifest + hashed prompt IDs + routing metadata) and place it on the customer SFTP within 5 business days. Format: CSV manifest, gzipped payload, SHA256 checksums.

Attachments I will produce: redline-responses.docx (answers to their redlines), redlines_summary.xlsx (mapping of each Catalyst redline to our position and required action).

Ops notes for Dylan: please plan for onshore KMS key scoping if Catalyst insists on key residency; if not, we can route proof artifacts to Catalyst SFTP in US-East. Also add a short note on ephemeral KV retention windows (default 48 hrs) and how we can reduce to 24 on request.

I'll assemble the artifacts once Dylan confirms the SFTP sample format and KMS feasibility.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Privacy & Trust — Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lee <sara.lee@catalysthealth.com>, procurement@catalysthealth.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ML usage & DPA: opt-out evidence and export routing

Sara — following up with concrete answers and next steps below. Apologies for the longer note, wanted to be explicit for procurement.

Summary answers:
- "No-train" scope: Redwood will not use Catalyst tenant content to update public foundation model weights or to feed into automated customer-facing fine-tuning pipelines. We will continue to collect system health telemetry (aggregate/anonymized) by default; suppression of telemetry is available as a paid configuration.

- Prompt/response ownership: We accept the addendum language proposed by Kimberly. We'll include: "Customer retains ownership of prompts and generated outputs where Customer has expressly opted into 'Customer output ownership' in the Ordering Document; otherwise standard Redwood output license applies."

- Evidence & delivery: Redwood will provide both: (A) signed attestation within 3 business days after DPA addendum acceptance; (B) one-time SFTP export sample within 5 business days. The sample will include a CSV manifest, hashed prompt IDs, timestamps, routing metadata, gzipped payloads, and checksums. We can run the export to Catalyst's secure SFTP endpoint (please provide connection details) or to an onshore temporary bucket we will share with you.

Requested items from your side to meet the Jan 5 procurement target:
1) Confirm which evidence route you prefer: SFTP to Catalyst or onshore temporary bucket.
2) Provide the SFTP connection (hostname, user, key) or request Redwood's temporary bucket.
3) Confirm whether you want telemetry collection suppressed completely (separate SOW) or the standard reduced retention (we can set to 24 hrs).

Attachments included for your review: redline-responses.docx (answers to each redline), redlines_summary.xlsx (position matrix).

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4521), DocuSign signature placeholder (https://www.docusign.com/en/link/example-signature-req)

If those items look good I'll get Legal to finalize the DPA addendum and Ops will schedule the SFTP export once we have your endpoint. Happy to hop on a 20-min call tomorrow afternoon if that helps.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Most-Trusted Integrations, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134
